title: Ashtpadi 10, salok: countless
hookLine: the salok marvels at countless beings

cards: Rush hour at a train station. A flood of people, every one the main character of their own story. One is late for a job interview.
One just got engaged. One is going to visit a mother in the hospital. One is humming.
You'll never know any of them, and each carries an inner life as large as yours. A crowd like that can make a person feel very small, or strangely tender.
For several ashtpadis, Sukhmani has zoomed in on one kind of person. Now it pulls back, and looks at the crowd.

teach.b: The salok of ashtpadi ten has two lines. The first: ustat karahi anek jan. Countless people sing His praise.
Ustat is praise; anek is many, more than one can number.
And there's no end to it: ant na paaraavaar, no near bank or far bank.

teach.h: RACHNAA: A CREATION OF MANY KINDS.
teach.b: The second line: Nanak, God made the creation in so many ways, of countless kinds. Rachnaa is creation, the thing made, the way a poem or a building is made. Bahu bidh, many ways.
Anik prakaar, countless kinds. Notice what's being praised. Not one perfect person, not the brahm giaanee of two ashtpadis ago, but the sheer number and variety of what exists.

In the stanzas that follow, Guru Arjan will list them: people who worship and people who wander, scholars and the lost, worlds beyond worlds. The salok sets the tone for all of it, and the tone is wonder. So many.
When you really take that in, something shifts.
Your own problems are still real, but they're one story among millions.
The people who annoy you are also among the so many, each with a whole inner life. And the One who made the creation in all those ways is, the salok says, beyond any shore you could reach.
Here the crowd isn't a reason to feel lost. It's a reason for wonder, and everyone in it is part of the same creation.

how: Sikhs reading Sukhmani Sahib meet this salok at the opening of the tenth ashtpadi, whose stanzas go on to list the countless beings of the creation.

o: the creation, the thing that is made
the far shore no one can reach

games.q: the tenth salok — tap the pairs.

s: the salok praises one perfect person
it marvels at countless people and a creation of countless kinds.
the salok says the praise has no far shore
ant na paaraavaar: no end, no near bank or far bank.
rachnaa means creation, the thing made
made in many ways, of countless kinds.

games.q: you're in a huge crowd and feel tiny. by the tenth salok, what's another way to see it?
o: you're one story among so many, all part of one creation.
everyone else matters less than you.
games.why: the salok's tone is wonder: so many, made in so many ways.

practice: Look out a window at people passing, or at faces in a photo, or, eyes closed, picture a busy street you know, and pick out one stranger.

Imagine, just for a breath, that they too woke up this morning with worries and hopes, then another, then another, and let your face soften as you look. If you pray, you can wish them well in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Rachnaa, the creation, the thing made. Its salok marvels at countless people praising, and a rachnaa made in so many ways.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: rachnaa, creation, the thing made; God made it, the salok says, in countless kinds.

carryVoice: Your line: so many. Every one of them a whole story, and all of it one creation. See you tomorrow.

sources.work: Guru Granth Sahib (Guru Arjan, Gauri Sukhmani)
